recommendedZaStudioRevision.label: Bilingual software & design studio
recommendedZaStudioRevision.description: A bilingual studio website with perspective-driven project navigation, per-project brand palettes, four themes, and reusable case studies combining galleries, architecture diagrams, and product stories.
recommendedZaStudioRevision.overview: Za Studio is the shared software-and-design studio website for Ahmed Magdy and Zeyad Salama. Its identity carries through a CSS 3D project staircase, layered route transitions, per-project palettes, and four coordinated themes. A typed bilingual content system builds case studies from galleries, architecture diagrams, metrics, and editorial blocks; Arabic layouts, keyboard access, and reduced-motion behavior are part of the implementation.

highlights.title: A studio identity in motion
highlights.description: Perspective typography, project stairs, layered navigation, and theme-aware illustrations make the identity part of the browsing experience.

highlights.title: One content system, many stories
highlights.description: Typed English and Arabic content drives reusable galleries, diagrams, metrics, quotes, and product sections, with a palette for each case study.

highlights.title: Responsive and motion-aware
highlights.description: Responsive routes, keyboard controls, Arabic text direction, and reduced-motion fallbacks support the same work across devices and visitor preferences.

correctionsToStudioClaims: China ERP portfolio should retain company-wide shared records; Za Studio text says tenant-isolated but the local backend ADR supersedes that design.
RealState frontend currently contains landing/auth only. Za Studio admin screenshots and marketing descriptions must not be treated as evidence of the inspected client implementation.
FEI studio screenshots are explicitly rebuilt from a team design; label as reconstructed references if ever reused, not fresh original frontend captures.
XDisplay studio media are illustrations, not application screenshots; keep that distinction if ever reused.
